objections.claim: The merge controller binds required-check evidence only to the publisher-captured PR head SHA, but `pull_request` Actions normally evaluate GitHub's synthetic test-merge commit. GitHub specifies that when this test-merge commit has a status, that commit—not the source head—must pass ([required-check documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks)); `GITHUB_SHA` likewise identifies the PR merge branch commit ([event documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows)). Consequently, E1 can either reject valid PRs because no required runs exist at the source head or authenticate a run that did not test the merge candidate. `strict:true` only makes the server refuse the eventual PUT; it does not repair this oracle. The controller must bind the source head and current base to the API-derived test-merge SHA, verify that merge commit's parents, authenticate required runs at the SHA GitHub actually selected, and include a regression where source-head and test-merge SHAs differ.
